steps.title: Start with every supplier on file
steps.change: `Suppliers` is the first `FROM` source because every supplier on file must appear, including Gamma even though it has no order lines. These three master rows are the report's required supplier population; the later FULL OUTER JOIN adds unknown IDs found only in order lines.

steps.title: Preserve order lines as well as suppliers
steps.change: Add `OrderDetails` second because its `SupplierID` is the key needed to attach quantities and expose IDs missing from the supplier master. The key is available directly in both sources. FULL OUTER JOIN is required: IDs 1 and 2 match; order-line ID 99 survives with NULL supplier columns; Gamma survives with NULL order-line columns. The two Alpha lines repeat its supplier columns because two details match.
steps.added_sql:
FULL OUTER JOIN OrderDetails AS OD
    ON S.SupplierID = OD.SupplierID
steps.sql:
SELECT S.SupplierID AS supplier_id, S.CompanyName AS company_name,
       OD.OrderDetailID, OD.SupplierID AS order_supplier_id, OD.Quantity
FROM Suppliers AS S
FULL OUTER JOIN OrderDetails AS OD
    ON S.SupplierID = OD.SupplierID
ORDER BY COALESCE(S.SupplierID, OD.SupplierID), OD.OrderDetailID;

steps.title: Resolve the identity and fallback label
steps.change: The joined rows still have two possible identity columns. `COALESCE` chooses the master SupplierID when present and otherwise the order-line SupplierID; it also supplies `Unknown supplier` for ID 99. This is a row-preserving projection: five joined rows remain five.
steps.added_sql:
COALESCE(S.SupplierID, OD.SupplierID) AS SupplierID,
COALESCE(S.CompanyName, 'Unknown supplier') AS CompanyName
steps.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(S.SupplierID, OD.SupplierID) AS SupplierID,
       COALESCE(S.CompanyName, 'Unknown supplier') AS CompanyName,
       OD.OrderDetailID, OD.Quantity
FROM Suppliers AS S
FULL OUTER JOIN OrderDetails AS OD
    ON S.SupplierID = OD.SupplierID
ORDER BY COALESCE(S.SupplierID, OD.SupplierID), OD.OrderDetailID;

steps.title: Group detail rows into one supplier result
steps.change: Group by the resolved identity and display name. The two Alpha detail rows contribute 2 + 3 = 5; Beta contributes 5; unknown ID 99 contributes 4. Gamma's preserved unmatched row has NULL Quantity, so SUM is NULL before the learner's COALESCE changes the displayed units to zero. Four supplier groups remain.
steps.added_sql:
COALESCE(SUM(OD.Quantity), 0) AS units_supplied
GROUP BY resolved SupplierID, resolved CompanyName
steps.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(S.SupplierID, OD.SupplierID) AS SupplierID,
       COALESCE(S.CompanyName, 'Unknown supplier') AS CompanyName,
       COALESCE(SUM(OD.Quantity), 0) AS units_supplied
FROM Suppliers AS S
FULL OUTER JOIN OrderDetails AS OD
    ON S.SupplierID = OD.SupplierID
GROUP BY COALESCE(S.SupplierID, OD.SupplierID),
         COALESCE(S.CompanyName, 'Unknown supplier')
ORDER BY units_supplied DESC;

steps.title: Prepare the all-order-line denominator
steps.change: The `sum_quantity` CTE is an independent one-row aggregate over every OrderDetails row. Its one CTE row represents the grand total (2 + 3 + 5 + 4 = 14), not a supplier. The outer query still starts from the four supplier groups; its scalar subquery attaches the same denominator to each group. This branch is independent of the supplier lookup and can be prepared separately.
steps.added_sql:
WITH sum_quantity AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(Quantity), 0) AS total_quantity
    FROM OrderDetails
)
-- scalar lookup: (SELECT total_quantity FROM sum_quantity)
steps.sql:
WITH sum_quantity AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(Quantity), 0) AS total_quantity
    FROM OrderDetails
)
SELECT SupplierID, CompanyName, units_supplied,
       (SELECT total_quantity FROM sum_quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM (
    SELECT COALESCE(S.SupplierID, OD.SupplierID) AS SupplierID,
           COALESCE(S.CompanyName, 'Unknown supplier') AS CompanyName,
           COALESCE(SUM(OD.Quantity), 0) AS units_supplied
    FROM Suppliers AS S
    FULL OUTER JOIN OrderDetails AS OD ON S.SupplierID = OD.SupplierID
    GROUP BY COALESCE(S.SupplierID, OD.SupplierID),
             COALESCE(S.CompanyName, 'Unknown supplier')
) AS supplier_totals
ORDER BY units_supplied DESC;

steps.title: Calculate shares and apply the requested order
steps.change: The exact saved learner query calculates each group's units × 100 ÷ 14, rounds to two decimals, returns 0.00 when the denominator is zero, and sorts by units descending. The four rows reconcile to 14 units. Alpha and Beta tie at five, so their relative order is intentionally not asserted.
steps.added_sql:
ROUND(units_supplied * 100.0 / total_quantity, 2)
-- CASE returns 0.00 when total_quantity = 0
ORDER BY units_supplied DESC

validation_cases.name: No order lines: all suppliers remain at zero
Unknown and NULL supplier IDs both survive as distinct groups
All quantities zero: denominator guard returns zero shares
